title: A Genuine Narrative of the Deplorable Deaths of the English Gentlemen, and Others, who Were Suffocated in the Black-Hole in Fort-William, at Calcutta, in the Kingdom of Bengal, in the Night Succeeding the 20th Day of June, 1756, in a Letter to a Friend
note: John Zephaniah Holwell's first-person account, published in London for A. Millar in 1758. The title page identifies the work as a letter to a friend and dates the episode to the night succeeding 20 June 1756. Publication details verified against the title page and Google Books catalog; this is participant testimony, not independent corroboration of its figures or conclusions.
subcategory: Participant accounts of the 1756 fall of Calcutta
whyItMatters: Holwell was a survivor and participant, so his narrative records how he represented the confinement to readers in Britain. Its casualty count and attribution of responsibility are claims by one interested witness and require independent corroboration.
